relevance_note: Case report of an adolescent with a GFAP variant plus a comparison table of six earlier-published carriers: 'Whole exome sequencing revealed an extremely rare missense GFAP heterozygous variant NM_002055.5: c.54G>T (p/Gly18Val), confirming the diagnosis of AxD'.
method_note: Read the full paper by hand. Tables 2 and 3 (patients as columns; column header row: 'Symptom/Feature | Our Patient | Patient I:2 | Patient II:2 | Patient II:3 | Patient II:5 | Patient III:4 | Patient III:5') were transcribed by a short Python script that splits each row and builds row-label-through-cell spans; output was checked against the tables. 'Our Patient' is a role word, so the case is labelled 'patient' (rule 5); the six earlier-published family members from Casasnovas et al. [17] use the paper's labels and source_reference_in_review = the References row cell '[17]'. Literature patients: sex, age at onset, age of diagnosis and features from Tables 2-3; 'NA' and 'Not reported' cells left not reported; 'No' cells (a word, not a symbol) recorded as excluded. Ages in Table 2 have no unit; ISO durations assume years. Their variant (p/Gly18Val, heterozygous, missense) comes from the Table 2 caption naming the patients in the table; cDNA left null because the literature-review text gives c.53G>T for Casasnovas' six adults but cites reference [7] (Paprocka et al.) rather than [17], while this patient is c.54G>T and the paper calls them 'the same variant/mutation'. CONTRADICTIONS: (1) c.54G>T (this patient) vs c.53G>T (Casasnovas adults) for the 'same variant' p/Gly18Val; Casasnovas cited as [7] in Section 3.2 and [17] elsewhere. (2) Ataxia: Table 2 gives 'Mild' for our patient, but the text says coordination was preserved and lists 'evident cerebellar ataxia' among absent features; both rows emitted, checklist ataxia not reported. (3) Bulbar symptoms: Table 2 gives Yes/Subtle for all six Casasnovas patients, while the Discussion says neither the familial case nor our patient exhibited bulbar symptoms and notes a 'consistent absence of bulbar and autonomic involvement'; the text's group reference is ambiguous, so only table rows emitted. (4) Table 2 'Neurocognitive deficits: No' for the six vs text 'No information regarding intellectual decline was available for the reported six patients'; excluded table rows kept, checklist cognitive decline left not reported for them. (5) Patients II:3 and II:5: 'Bladder dysfunction: Yes' but 'Dysautonomia: No'; checklist autonomic dysfunction (which includes bladder dysfunction) set not reported for them. (6) Text says oculomotor abnormalities were reported in all other carriers, but Table 2 gives 'Not reported' for Patient I:2 (left not reported). (7) Spastic paraparesis 'No' for I:2 and II:2 vs Section 3.2 'six adults with slowly progressive spastic paraparesis' (cited [7]); table values kept. Our patient's brain and cervical MRI were first read as normal and re-read after the genetic diagnosis as showing medulla and anterior cervical cord signal abnormalities; the re-read is recorded. Cerebral white matter, contrast enhancement, basal ganglia and periventricular rim left not reported (initial 'otherwise normal' brain MRI was later revised; no explicit statement). Head circumference 54 cm (10th percentile) not recorded as macrocephaly/its absence. Normal-finding rule (D-27): whole-exam normals (ophthalmologic examination and funduscopy, NCS/EMG, ECG/echocardiography, plasma/urine amino-acid profiles) are written as the paper names them, without more specific exclusions. Infectious screening and the negative HSP panel, MLD and VLCFA tests were not recorded as features. n_patients_reported and cites_prior_report_of_same_patients left null: the authors give no total, and the earlier-published patients are captured through source_reference_in_review. No stacked ' / ' cells in this paper.
